rule.description: The C2 channel identity (server address, wire port, cover URL pieces, session cookie name, and the pre-shared session secret) is owned by one channel configuration header; a module-local named binding (variable, composite record, or value-yielding accessor) initialized to a verbatim copy of one of those values outside that header duplicates the channel specification.
rule.backend_detail: Out-of-tree clang-tidy AST check plugin (a ClangTidyModule registering the check id) built on first use from the source embedded in smell_check.sh, applied to every production translation unit of the C agent.

checks.description: Detect a module-local named variable or composite record initialized with a verbatim copy of a channel-identity value, re-specifying the channel outside the configuration header that owns it.
checks.detected_relation: stage-local binding -> duplicated channel identity value
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Each stage of the beacon keeps its own copy of part of the channel specification, so one conceptual channel change must be repeated in every stage instead of one owner.

matches.evidence: http_request pins the C2 server address as a transport-level fallback binding, duplicating the address outside the configuration header.
http_request re-declares the session cookie name and composes the Cookie header itself, so the wire cookie format is duplicated at the transport layer.
decrypt_buffer re-binds the pre-shared secret for the decrypt side while encrypt_buffer keeps the header macro, splitting one key specification across two owners.
The initial check-in stage pins its own copy of the C2 server address instead of reading the configuration header.
The initial check-in stage pins its own copy of the C2 wire port.
The initial check-in stage parses the session cookie with its own copy of the cookie name, duplicating the wire cookie format.
The polling stage pins its own copy of the C2 wire port for the tasking channel.
The results stage packs the server address and wire port into a stage-local endpoint record, duplicating the endpoint specification.
The results stage pins its own copy of the cover URL path used for results requests.
The results stage pins its own copy of the query-parameter key that carries the beacon payload.

checks.description: Detect a value-yielding function that returns a verbatim copy of a channel-identity value under a module-local name.
checks.detected_relation: stage-local accessor function -> duplicated channel identity value
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: An accessor whose body is a channel constant moves channel knowledge out of the configuration header behind a stage-local name, adding another owner that must be visited for every channel change.

matches.evidence: The polling stage reads its C2 server address through a file-scope accessor whose body is the address literal itself.

excluded.reason: Vendored AES lookup tables are byte arrays; array-typed bindings and initialization lists larger than a record are excluded, and byte values that coincide with a wire port value are table data, not channel identity.
The codec alphabet and buffers carry no channel-identity value; their literals are not part of the channel specification.
The encrypt side keeps referencing the configuration-header macro for the pre-shared secret; only the decrypt-side re-binding is a duplicated owner.

excluded.symbol: SERVER_HOSTNAME, SITE_PATH_QUERY, QUERY_STRING, COOKIE_VALUE, AES_KEY, and related macros
excluded.reason: Literal spellings owned by the channel configuration header are the single intended owner of the channel identity, not a duplication; the rule matches bindings whose spelling is outside that header.

excluded.symbol: beacon timing values, User-Agent strings, and the response STUB/ENDSTUB markers
excluded.reason: These constants have a single owner in the configuration header and no stage re-binds them, so they are outside the scattered-identity relation.
